## Practical AI in Engineering {#practical-ai-in-engineering}

**A case-study-driven open repository and course**

Led by **Bahareh Abdi (Abdikivanani)**, with **Gosia Migut, Tom Viering, Martin Sand, and Dario Turelli** as co-applicants, this project connects AI and machine learning methods with the decisions engineers face in practice. It received **€25,000 through TU Delft's AI-Augmented Engineering Education call in 2025**.

The team is developing reusable case studies and course materials with students and professional partners. Cases span areas including healthcare, finance, and sustainability. Coding activities and structured reflection help students work with imperfect data, competing stakeholder needs, and ethical questions as part of the same engineering problem.

Students practise defining problems with stakeholders, examining data quality and bias, evaluating models, and interpreting and communicating their results. The materials are being developed and tested, including pilots in the AI minor, with the aim of making them openly available for use across disciplines.

[Project update from TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/ai/education/ai-education-in-the-discipline) · [Funding and project team](https://www.microelectronics.tudelft.nl/eee/News/) · [2025 grant announcement](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/2025/delft-ai/four-new-grants-awarded-for-development-of-ai-augmented-engineering-education)

### TU Delft Education Team of the Year 2026 {#education-team-of-the-year-2026}

**Practical AI in Engineering received TU Delft's Education Team of the Year award**, celebrated at Education Day on **5 November 2026**.

The Teaching Academy recognised the collaboration across EEMCS, Aerospace Engineering, and Technology, Policy and Management. Its announcement highlighted the combination of technical AI learning, ethical reasoning, and authentic engineering challenges—and the team's ambition to build reusable resources that benefit education beyond a single course.

## The concepts that change how students see ML

**Lisa Zhang, Gosia Migut, and Jesse H. Krijthe · ITiCSE 2026**

This work investigates ideas that can transform students' understanding of machine learning. Five proposed concepts concern optimisation, balancing sources of error, empirical investigation, geometry, and probability. The community discussed how these perspectives can inform teaching on 1 October 2026.

[Presentation (PDF)](https://filelist.tudelft.nl/Websections/AIDU/Website%20ML%20Teachers%20Community/Documents/lunch1Oct26_GosiaJesse.pdf) · [Accompanying blog](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~lczhang/iticse2026/blog.html)

## Which comes first: models or applications?

**Ilinca Rențea · Presented 1 October 2026**

A study across TU Delft, the University of Toronto, and North Carolina State University involved 117 students in linear-regression workshops. It compared the order of model-focused and application-focused instruction, examining knowledge, motivation, and students' perceptions.

The preliminary findings presented in October did not show a statistically significant difference in knowledge or motivation between the conditions. Written responses suggested possible differences in how students framed the subject. These are preliminary findings, rather than a final conclusion about the best teaching sequence.

[Study presentation (PDF)](https://filelist.tudelft.nl/Websections/AIDU/Website%20ML%20Teachers%20Community/Documents/lunch1Oct26_Ilinca.pdf) · [Contact Ilinca](mailto:I.E.I.Rentea@tudelft.nl)

## The mathematics students need

**Matias Valdenegro Toro · University of Groningen**

A Senior University Teaching Qualification study, discussed at the October gathering, examined mathematical prerequisites for ML teaching: calculus, linear algebra, probability, and statistics.

[Find the October gathering](index.qmd#event-archive)

## Education Fellowship 2026

**Gosia Migut and Tom Viering**

Their Education Fellowship project develops the next steps for the AI teaching community. It connects shared teaching materials through CAIT with community exchange and small educational projects, helping teachers build on each other's work across faculties.

[Read the TU Delft fellowship announcement](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/ai/research-innovation/ai-awards-grants) · [Explore micro-grant projects](micro-grant-projects.qmd)
